head.title: SQL Island Sequel- Isle of Architects (T1)
head.teaser: Island of Architects: The Quest for the hidden Data (MIN, MAX, ANY)
head.copyright: Ansari Sadaf Ambreen Shamim, Lars Kehrle, Anna Król, Fabian Lieb, Luc Stoffer. © CC BY 4.0

text-scene.text: As the engines of the escape plane roared to life, the coastline of SQL Island finally began to shrink into the horizon. But the celebration was short-lived; a sudden, localized electromagnetic storm—a “Data Surge”—fried the navigation systems, and the plane is forced into an emergency descent.

Far beyond the usual networks and databases, in the middle of the Digital Ocean, lies a mysterious land known as Isle of Architects 🌴 This island was created long ago by the legendary Data Architects, who hid powerful knowledge inside ancient data tables scattered across the island. Only those who understand the language of SQL can unlock its secrets.

Now, while the pilot tries to fix the failed systems, your mission is to explore the island, uncover hidden records, and find out what caused your crash. To get back into the air, you must prove you’ve moved beyond the basics.

The Data Architects left behind advanced trials that must be completed before any explorer can escape. These trials introduce deeper concepts of data analysis and comparison — powerful MIN(), MAX(), and ANY.
MIN() – Reveal the smallest value in a dataset MAX() – Reveal the greatest value in a dataset ANY – Compare a value against a group of values Your adventure begins now!

Challenge 1 – The Oldest Wisdom
You arrive at the Great Library of SQL Island, a quiet place filled with ancient books containing records of the island’s past. The Librarian, one of the oldest members of the Order of Query Masters, greets you.
“Welcome, young Data Explorer. If you wish to understand SQL Island, you must first learn about the Data Architects who built it.”

He points to a dusty "book" titled `EXPLORERS`: “Somewhere in this book are the names of the oldest explorers who ever walked SQL Island. If you can find them, you will uncover the greatest wisdom recorded in our archives.”

select-scene.text: You need to "open" the "book" in order to inspect records of the island’s past. Hint: Display the complete table `EXPLORERS`
Hint: Search the table `EXPLORERS` and find all explorers whose age is the maximum age recorded in the table.

text-scene.text: Well done, Explorer! You’ve unlocked a key insight! You learned how to find extreme values using MAX() and compare all rows to that result. This helps identify top records in a dataset.

Challenge 2 – The Youngest Apprentice
After discovering the oldest explorers, the Librarian smiles and flips through the EXPLORERS book again, pointing to the newest entries.

“Some of our newest members are even babies, younger than the apprentices. But your task is to find the youngest apprentice. Knowing who holds this title will help you understand how the Order continues its legacy.”

select-scene.text: Hint: Search the EXPLORERS table and find the explorers with the minimum age among those with the rank Apprentice.
select-scene.sql-solution: WITH Apprentices AS ( SELECT * FROM EXPLORERS WHERE rank = 'Apprentice' ) SELECT * FROM Apprentices WHERE age = (SELECT MIN(age) FROM Apprentices);

text-scene.text: Impressive move! You’re thinking like a true Architect. You practiced filtering data first, then applying MIN() on a specific group. This shows how to narrow scope before calculating values.

Challenge 3 - The Gateway of Comparison
Leaving the Great Library behind, you continue deeper into SQL Island. The stone path leads you to an ancient structure known as the Gateway of Comparison. The gate is guarded by a silent stone statue of one of the original Data Architects.

As you approach, glowing runes appear on the gate.
"Only explorers who have proven themselves stronger than the apprentices may pass."

A stone tablet emerges from the ground displaying records from the EXPLORERS table. The message continues:
“Find all explorers whose age is greater than any apprentice of the Order. Those who surpass even the youngest apprentices may step through the gateway.”

select-scene.text: Hint: To unlock the gate, you must compare explorers against the ages of all apprentices using one of the ancient SQL spells.
select-scene.sql-solution: SELECT * FROM EXPLORERS WHERE age > ANY ( SELECT age FROM EXPLORERS WHERE rank = 'Apprentice' );

text-scene.text: Great work! Your query skills are getting sharper. You learned how to compare a value against multiple options using ANY. This makes filtering across several categories easier.

Challenge 4 - The Hall of Balance
After passing through the Gateway of Comparison, you enter a hidden chamber deep beneath the Island: the Hall of Balance. Two ancient crystals float above a stone pedestal. One glows with the energy of the youngest Scout, the other with the wisdom of the oldest Scout.

An inscription appears on the wall: “Only those whose age lies within the balance of the Scouts may continue. Not younger than the youngest. Not older than the oldest.” The pedestal reveals records from the EXPLORERS table.

select-scene.text: Hint: Your task is to find all explorers whose age lies between the minimum and maximum age of all Scouts, including the boundary ages themselves. This means you must first discover the youngest Scout and the oldest Scout, then find every explorer whose age falls within that full range.
select-scene.sql-solution: SELECT * FROM EXPLORERS WHERE age >= ( SELECT MIN(age) FROM EXPLORERS WHERE rank = 'Scout' ) AND age <= ( SELECT MAX(age) FROM EXPLORERS WHERE rank = 'Scout' );

text-scene.text: Excellent! You’ve passed another trial of logic. You learned how to define a range using MIN() and MAX() and filter values within it. This helps analyze data within boundaries.

Challenge 5 - The Mirror of Equality After leaving the Hall of Balance, you enter a quiet circular chamber illuminated by a floating crystal mirror. The chamber is known among the Order as "The Mirror of Equality".

As you approach, glowing runes appear on the mirror:
“Balance alone is not enough. Only those whose wisdom equals the greatest among the Scouts may continue deeper into SQL Island.”

select-scene.text: Hint: A stone console appears and displays records from the `EXPLORERS` table. Your task is to determine the "oldest Scout" and find all explorers whose age is equal to that value. This means you must: - Determine the maximum age among all Scouts - Find every explorer whose age equals that value
select-scene.sql-solution: SELECT * FROM EXPLORERS WHERE age = ( SELECT MAX(age) FROM EXPLORERS WHERE rank = 'Scout' );

text-scene.text: Nicely done! You’re reading the data with precision. You reinforced how to combine filtering with MAX() to find the top value inside a specific group. This is useful for targeted comparisons.
The mirror glows brightly and slowly rotates, revealing a hidden passage deeper into the island.

Challenge 6 - The Architects’ Ledger
Ahead of you are a set of stairs. Descending deeper, you discover a secret chamber known as the Core Chamber of the Architects. Here, the island is no longer fragmented into trials or puzzles, it is a place where the Order of Query Masters regulates data.

In front of you a massive stone table covered in glowing inscriptions. You see that the glowing inscriptions on the table show new records - Mission Logs (`MISSION_LOGS`). - Each query executed by explorers produces a measurable power draw (`power_draw`). - Some executions are safe, but others produce unstable spikes that the system flags as anomalous.

select-scene.text: First, you need to read this notes to understand what is related and what is not. Hint: Display the complete table `MISSION_LOGS`

text-scene.text:
When that total becomes too high, the system activates a safety mechanism: an automatic voltage relay that generates an electromagnetic barrier, isolating the island from outside navigation.
This maybe the real reason of your plane’s crash!

You need to find it out and identify which explorers are responsible for the strongest execution bursts. The idea is not just to look at single logs, but to understand each explorer’s peak behaviour across all their activity.

select-scene.text: Hint: Use the tables EXPLORERS and MISSION_LOGS to find all explorers whose single strongest execution is more extreme than at least one recorded anomaly
select-scene.sql-solution: WITH ExplorerPeaks AS ( SELECT explorer_id, MAX(power_draw) AS max_power FROM MISSION_LOGS GROUP BY explorer_id ) SELECT ep.*, e.name, e.rank FROM ExplorerPeaks ep JOIN EXPLORERS e ON ep.explorer_id = e.explorer_id WHERE ep.max_power > ANY ( SELECT power_draw FROM MISSION_LOGS WHERE anomalous = TRUE );

text-scene.text: Solid progress! You’re moving deeper into the system. You learned how to combine GROUP BY with MAX() to find peak values per explorer, then compare them using ANY. This helps detect who exceeds critical thresholds across grouped data.

The result reveals three explorers who stand out. At first, this looks like the full story. These are the largest recorded surges, and together they already seem close to system limits. For a moment, it seems like the problem is solved. But the system does not react. There is no restart.

Challenge 7 - The Black Box Revelation
Then a new message appears on the stone surface: “Even if those peak values are considered, the total still does not exceed the system’s global safety threshold. Something is still missing. Some executions that look normal can be actually dangerous, but were never marked as anomalous.

select-scene.text: Hint: You need to search for all non-anomalous activity that still falls inside that same dangerous corridor. Use the table MISSION_LOGS and in between values.
select-scene.sql-solution: SELECT m.*,e.name, e.rank FROM MISSION_LOGS m JOIN EXPLORERS e ON m.explorer_id = e.explorer_id WHERE power_draw BETWEEN (SELECT MIN(power_draw) FROM MISSION_LOGS WHERE anomalous = TRUE) AND (SELECT MAX(power_draw) FROM MISSION_LOGS WHERE anomalous = TRUE) AND anomalous = FALSE;

text-scene.text: Outstanding! You’re proving worthy of the Architects’ knowledge. You learned how to use MIN() and MAX() to define a danger range and apply BETWEEN to find hidden cases. This reveals inconsistencies where data looks safe but actually falls within risky limits.
Here comes the second discovery — one execution was not marked as dangerous. This changes everything. The system was pushed past its limit not by three spikes, but by four.
The relay activated because of the real total load, but only three spikes were recorded. Because of that, the system never fully confirmed the shutdown in its logs.

And when the system later “returned to safe state” on paper, it never actually deactivated the electromagnetic barrier around the island. The isolation remained active, trapping navigation systems and causing your plane to lose control.

A message suddenly appears on the stone surface: “System inconsistency detected. Total power recalculated. System registered the real overload. Stabilization in progress. Protection layer shutting down. Electromagnetic barrier deactivated.”
The navigation systems of your plane come back online. The mist around the island begins to lift, and not because anything in the world changed, but because your understanding did.
As you board the repaired plane, the Order of Query Masters delivers its final message: “Those who master data do not escape systems. They see through them”
The pilot starts the engine. The Island fades into the Digital Ocean below—no longer a mystery, but a map you now understand how to read.

Congratulations! You've solved all the puzzles! We hope that, you’ve learned how to analyze data from multiple angles—finding extremes with MIN() and MAX(), filtering specific groups, comparing values with ANY, and working within ranges using BETWEEN.
